item.title: Singing Arts Workshop with Keith Little and Helen Foley — Sun Nov 1, 11:00 AM — Art and Music Gallery
item.description:
Learn the art of singing from two exceptional musicians, vocalists, and teachers at this one-day workshop on November 1, from 11am-6pm at the Art and Music Gallery, 824 Petaluma Blvd. South. A light lunch is included.
This workshop will take your singing to a new level, focusing on the beautiful vocals in acoustic bluegrass music. Keith Little has more than 50 years of experience in the worldwide acoustic music scene. Helen Foley has more than 15 years performing nationally and internationally with award-winning musicians. She has a particular love for bluegrass harmony singing. Keith has been hosting his Singing Arts workshop in the Bay area since 2006. Both are members of the California Bluegrass Association. For more information and registration details, email Betty Bugaj at bkbugaj@icloud.com.
Source: North Bay Bohemian

item.title: Valley Queen — Thu Nov 5, 6:00 PM — Little Saint
item.description:
Propelled by Natalie Carol’s "bracingly afflicted, mountain-vaulting dream-country yodel" \(Rolling Stone\), Valley Queen reemerges, flush with recognizable vocal power and newly advanced emotional resonance in the new single “Falling.”
Whereas their 2018 debut Supergiant dealt in the nostalgic language of rock, Valley Queen’s new music is borne of the endless present Carol experienced in her bedroom during lockdown, where time collapsed and the future needed to be created. Longtime member Neil Wogensen’s deft studio production elevates Carol’s most intimate musings to a cosmic scale, while Mike Deluccia’s pristine and exuberant percussion and synth arrangements hold it all down with pulsating immediacy. The result is a mystical space where past, present, and future collapse; a forward-looking, starry-souled record whose vocal approach recalls the choral harmonies of Judee Sill, supported by arrangements with a dancing spiritual fixation on rhythm in league with the Cocteau Twins.
Va

item.title: Monica Da Silva & Complicated Animals — Fri Nov 6, 8:00 PM — The Saint
item.description:
Monica da Silva grew up living between The United States and Belém, Brazil, a city on the Amazon River. A love of travel and foreign language helped to forge her unique sound.
Paralleling her life, da Silva's music contains an eclectic mix of Brazilian and American influences. Her sound can be classified as International Fusion, as it is heavily influenced by Brazilian music, namely Bossa Nova, but also incorporates elements of Lounge, Electronica, Indie Pop, and Worldbeat. Da Silva brings her cultural diversity to her songs, smoothly flowing between English, Portuguese, and Spanish.
In 2010, da Silva released her album "Brasilissima" . The record featured songs in both of her native languages - English and Portuguese. The first single "Aí Então", “was chosen by Putumayo World Music to be included on their compilation “Brazilian Beat”. item.title: Gian Achen — Sat Nov 7, 4:30 PM — Wylde Provisions Co. (Playground & Café)
item.description:
Hailing from the eclectic streets of Berkeley, CA, Gian Achen is a singer-songwriter whose music blends nostalgic melodies with heartfelt lyrics. Growing up in the shadow of the Bay Area's rich musical history, Gian's sound is rooted in the golden era of '60s rock, drawing inspiration from iconic bands like The Beatles and Creedence Clearwater Revival as well as modern artists such as Wilco, The Shins, and The Cactus Blossoms. With a style that feels both timeless and fresh, Gian's music invites listeners to join him in a world that’s both familiar and uniquely his own.
Source: North Bay Bohemian

item.title: Wine Country Marine Corps Birthday Ball — Sat Nov 7, 5:30 PM — Jacuzzi Family Vineyards
item.description:
Brigadier General Andrew T. Priddy, Commanding General of the 1st Marine Division, based at Camp Pendleton in Southern California, will be Guest of Honor at Wine Country Marines’ 2026 Marine Corps Birthday Ball. The November 7 event at Jacuzzi Family Vineyards will celebrate the Corps’ 251st birthday.
Sonoma Valley’s annual event began in 1985. A formal Marine Corps Birthday Ball is an unusual gathering for a community as small as Sonoma, and its setting in the heart of California Wine Country has helped it become known as a “Destination Ball,” drawing Marines from across the country.
The local event is part of the worldwide Marine Corps Birthday Ball tradition honoring the Corps’ founding on November 10, 1775. Marines gather around that date each year to celebrate their shared history and service.

item.description:
Late Fall Kirtan Ecstatica: Kiranjot, Joss Jaffe & Isaac Rain
Join Kiranjot, Joss Jaffe and Isaac Rain for a joyful, devotional experience where sacred mantra meets global rhythm.
This is non-traditional Kirtan: the main language is English, making it accessible and inclusive, yet the music is deeply rooted in the rich tradition of Hindustani classical music, where devotion and practice invite you to merge into divine presence.
